picks.file: View of the Aleksandr Cannon Factory from the south in 1803.png
picks.what: The Alexander Cannon Works and the town from the south, engraving in Benedikt Hermann’s account of the Petrozavodsk works
picks.why: general view of the ironworks the town grew around, with its houses and the lake behind; dark post and plank at lower left trimmed

picks.what: The town center seen from the Zareka district, photograph
picks.why: general view across the town to the cathedral group; empty sky trimmed

picks.what: View over the wooden town during the Finnish occupation, photograph
picks.why: overview of the town from a height toward Lake Onega; top trimmed to cut text showing through from the book page

gaps: P0–P2: only icons and church objects; P6: kept the 2022 aerial (candidates are a construction site and an office building)
notes: #3 is a scan of an engraving in I. F. Hermann (Benedikt Hermann), Описание Петрозаводского и Кончезерского заводов, St. Petersburg 1803; the engraving is public domain by age, though the uploader tagged the scan CC BY 4.0. #12: the Finnish name Äänislinna and ‘during the war’ date it to the 1941–44 occupation. Best postcard view (#13, Cathedral Square with the Gostiny Dvor and Holy Spirit Cathedral) was left out because it is dated only ‘before 1917’.
